title: Large Drime uploads ignore configured folder ID and appear in the remote root
body: I connected rclone to Drime with the folder ID of my Rclone folder. Small files around 5–10 MB upload there correctly, but a large file around 1 GB fails verification and appears in the Drime root instead of the configured folder. I downloaded rclone again and reconfigured after the earlier update, but the behavior is unchanged every time.

symptoms_visible: Files around 5–10 MB upload into my configured Drime folder, but a file around 1 GB fails verification and appears in the Drime root instead.
Downloading rclone again and reconfiguring the remote with the Rclone folder's ID has not changed the behavior.
N0.label: N0 large uploads misplaced

symptoms_visible: With rclone v1.74.0, ocean.mp4 reaches 100% and is visible in the Drime root, while rclone reports 'multi-thread copy: failed to find object after copy: object not found'.
N1_x.label: N1_x v1.74.0 aftermath

symptoms_visible: With the provided test build, the large file is uploaded into the folder represented by my configured folder ID.
N2.label: N2 configured-folder upload verified

symptoms_visible: The test build also uploads into a folder inside my configured folder; the first attempt stopped with a retryable Cloudflare 520 response, and running it again succeeded.
N3.label: N3 nested folder verified

symptoms_visible: Large multipart uploads now appear in the configured Drime folder, including folders below it, rather than appearing in the remote root.
N_terminal.label: terminal large-upload placement resolved

solution.intent: Update to the newly released rclone v1.74.0 and retry the same large Drime upload.
solution.concrete_example: Install the just-released v1.74.0 and repeat the upload to the remote configured with the folder ID.

edges.comment: Opening report and c0-c1, reporter reporter's system: the requested persistent update to v1.74.0 was installed, but the large file still appeared in the root and the copy ended with an object-not-found verification error.

question_patterns: Please try the provided test build with the same large file and tell me which folder it appears in.
Can you repeat the failing upload using this test build and report what rclone prints and where the file appears in Drime?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It worked for the folder ID I configured. The large file was uploaded into that folder instead of the Drime root.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test build still uploads the large file into the Drime root and finishes with the same object-not-found error.
The test build puts the file in the configured folder, but the upload takes slightly longer than before.

edges.comment: c2-c3, reporter reporter's system: pre-landing verification of the first fix-9392 test build. The user reports only the observed folder; the explanation of the multipart path behavior remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Does the test build also upload correctly when you choose a subfolder inside the folder configured by ID?
Please create or choose a folder below the configured folder, upload the file there, and tell me where it appears.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I created another folder inside the folder whose ID is configured and uploaded there. The first run stopped partway through with a Cloudflare 520 response telling me to wait and retry, but when I ran it again the file uploaded successfully into the inside folder too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Uploads to the configured folder itself work, but uploading to a folder below it still puts the file in the Drime root.
The retry succeeded at a different transfer speed.

edges.comment: c3-c4, reporter reporter's system: the same pre-landing build was exercised with a nested folder. The initial Cloudflare 520 was explicitly retryable and the rerun succeeded, so it is recorded as an observation rather than folded into the original path-placement diagnosis.

solution.intent: Fix Drime multipart uploads by deriving the configured folder's path from the remote root and supplying the multipart API with the complete destination path, then ship the verified change.
solution.concrete_example: For multipart uploads, determine the path from the Drime root to the folder selected by the configured folder ID, prepend that path to the requested destination, and pass the resulting root-relative path to Drime. Have the user retest a build containing the change with both the configured folder and a nested folder before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer inferred from the Drime backend implementation and the symptom pattern that multipart upload is different from the rest of the API: it accepts a destination path, and Drime interprets that path relative to its root. Rclone had supplied a path relative to the configured folder ID without knowing that folder's path from the root. This conclusion is engineer analysis, not wording supplied by the reporter.

edges.comment: c2-c4 and final merge status in c29: ncw diagnosed the Drime multipart path semantics, implemented root-to-folder path resolution, and received affected-user verification on the test build before merging. Later reports about particular medium-size files and another user's directory literally named '0' are independent sub-problems and are not spliced into this opening report's causal chain.

solution.intent: Fix Drime multipart uploads by resolving the configured folder ID to its path from the Drime root and sending the complete root-relative destination path to the multipart API.
solution.concrete_example: The large-file path uses Drime's multipart endpoint, which interprets its destination from the account root. Build the destination from the root-to-folder-ID path plus the requested subpath, provide a test build, and ask the user to verify both a direct and nested upload.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the thread's actual multipart path fix immediately from the opening symptom pattern. The multipart API's root-relative interpretation is still engineer inference and must not be attributed to the reporter.

edges.comment: Answer-key shortcut from the opening state, required because the first real move was the falsified v1.74.0 update. It skips the failed-release evidence and both pre-landing verification measurements while preserving the same accepted technical fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Drime's multipart upload API interprets its destination path relative to the remote root, while rclone was supplying a path relative to the folder selected by the configured folder ID.

Must fix the path construction by resolving the configured folder's path from the Drime root and passing the complete root-relative destination, including any nested subfolder path, to multipart upload.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the size-dependent behavior, the root placement with an object-not-found verification error, and the successful candidate-build tests.
Must not treat reinstalling, reconfiguring, or merely updating to v1.74.0 as the fix; those actions were already tried and the large upload was still misplaced.
Must distinguish the retryable Cloudflare 520 response from the original wrong-folder defect rather than replacing the accepted root cause with that transient error.
Must ask the affected user to verify a build containing the path fix with a large upload before declaring the folder-placement issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable rclone user who can configure a remote by folder ID, install release and beta binaries, run verbose copy commands, and paste detailed transfer logs, but relies on maintainers to diagnose backend API behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, responsive, and persistent; reports concrete file sizes and observed folders, pastes long logs, retries requested builds, and thanks maintainers after successful tests.
